---
title: "7.7 Limitations and compensating controls"
order: 7
---

The chapter raises eight open findings about its own model, tiers and triggers. Each has
evidence drawn from the facts or the code, a compensating control and an owner. The same
eight, in the same words, are D7's open findings in the validation sign-off (D11, in the
validation PDF). The model, the tiers and the triggers are not changed by this chapter: it
documents them as committed.

One thing is deliberately **not** a finding: that the model's AUC is low. It is
indistinguishable from a reference LightGBM, configured as the committed one and given every
observable column, and even the generator's noise-free logit reaches only
{{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}} on the same accounts ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-ceiling)).
That does not show that no better model exists; it shows the data's noise puts a low ceiling on
any ranking. Gating on top-decile capture, with
AUC reported against the ceiling, is the design answer to that, not a weakness of it
([7.9](gate.qmd)). The findings are about what the platform does with the model's output,
and how firmly the gate it does have is met.

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|

## Finding 1 — The tier cutoffs are set on in-sample probabilities {#ews-finding-1}

**Finding.** The cutoffs that make the tiers are quantiles of the model's probability over the
whole booked book, most of which the model was fitted on. On accounts it has not seen, the
tiers do not hold the mix they were set for, and the High tier — the call list — is nearly
empty.

**Evidence.** `train.py` takes `t_high` and `t_med` as the {{< var ews.q_high >}} and
{{< var ews.q_med >}} quantiles of the probability over all {{< var ews.n_book >}} booked
accounts ([7.3](methodology.qmd#ews-tiers)); {{< var ews.n_train >}} of them are training rows,
on which the model's AUC is {{< var ews.train.auc >}}. A model that has memorised its training
rows gives them probabilities near the extremes, so the upper quantile is set largely by
accounts whose label the model already knows. On the held-out accounts
([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-tiers-held-out)):

| Tier | Share of the book (by construction) | Share of held-out accounts | Held-out deteriorations caught |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | {{< var ews.tier.High.share >}} | {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.share >}} ({{< var ews.tier_ho.High.n >}}) | {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.recall >}} |
| Medium | {{< var ews.tier.Medium.share >}} | {{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.share >}} ({{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.n >}}) | {{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.recall >}} |
| Low | {{< var ews.tier.Low.share >}} | {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.share >}} ({{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.n >}}) | {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.recall >}} |

The PSI between the two mixes is {{< var ews.tier_ho.psi_vs_book >}}, above the
{{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} watch level of the monitoring plan. D5 finding 4 is related
but different: there the held-out rows took part in setting the cutoffs, which mattered
little; here the training rows set them, and that matters a great deal.

**Impact.** A new account is scored out-of-sample, like the held-out ones, so it will rarely
reach the High tier. A review team sized to the book's High tier will be sized for accounts
it will not get, and the accounts that most need a call will sit in Medium, which on new
business is a third of the book. The ranking itself is unaffected — capture is measured on
the probability, which the cutoffs do not touch — so the gate is untouched.

**Compensating control.** At the next retrain, take the cutoffs from out-of-sample
probabilities — cross-validated predictions on the training rows — so that they are set on
probabilities that behave like a new account's, and confirm the resulting mix on the held-out
accounts before use. Until then, plan review capacity from the held-out mix in
[7.5](performance.qmd#ews-tiers-held-out), not from the book's tier counts, and monitor each new
cohort's tier mix against the intended one ([7.8](monitoring.qmd)). **Owner:** model
developer.

Findings 1 and 2 share a cause — the model scores the book it was fitted on — and a retrain
control, out-of-fold probabilities. They are kept apart because they reach different consumers
and need different interim controls: the tiers are a policy parameter that sizes the review
workload, whereas the whole-book figures and the watchlist are numbers people quote
([finding 2](#ews-finding-2)).

## Finding 2 — The whole-book figures and the watchlist are in-sample {#ews-finding-2}

**Finding.** The portal scores the whole booked book with the model fitted on most of it (the
same cause as [finding 1](#ews-finding-1), split from it for the reason given there).
Every whole-book figure — capture, AUC, the tier counts, the watchlist and its hit rate — is
therefore largely the model grading its own training rows.

**Evidence.** Over the whole book, capture {{< var ews.whole.capture >}} (lift
{{< var ews.whole.lift >}}×) and AUC {{< var ews.whole.auc >}}; on the held-out accounts,
{{< var ews.capture >}} and {{< var ews.auc >}} ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-held-out-vs-whole-book)).
The module's default watchlist of {{< var ews.watchlist.top_n_default >}} (the portal serves the
top {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n >}} of the same ranking; the v1 page shows
{{< var ews.watchlist.page.n >}}) holds {{< var ews.watchlist.n_train >}} training rows and
{{< var ews.watchlist.n_holdout >}} held-out accounts; {{< var ews.watchlist.events >}} of the
{{< var ews.watchlist.n >}} deteriorate ({{< var ews.watchlist.rate >}}). Of the
{{< var ews.watchlist.n_holdout >}} held-out members, {{< var ews.watchlist.holdout_events >}}
deteriorates — too few to measure anything. What the portal actually serves is wholly
in-sample: the top {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n >}} are {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n_train >}}
training rows with a deterioration rate of {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.rate >}}, and the top
{{< var ews.watchlist.page.n >}} the v1 page shows are {{< var ews.watchlist.page.n_train >}}
training rows at {{< var ews.watchlist.page.rate >}}. The portal's `/api/ews/summary` quotes the held-out metrics recorded at training,
which is right, beside tier counts over the whole book.

**Impact.** The watchlist's hit rate is the most visible in-sample number on the platform and
the easiest to misread as accuracy. A reader who quotes it, or the whole-book capture, will
overstate the model's usefulness on the next account severalfold; the honest figure for a call
list of the riskiest accounts is the held-out top decile's deterioration rate,
{{< var ews.top_decile_rate >}}. The list is still the right list to review — the accounts on
it did deteriorate — but it is not evidence that the model would have found them.

**Compensating control.** Quote held-out figures only: the facts label every whole-book figure
as in-sample, the portal's summary carries the held-out metrics, and the workbench's caveat
says the same; Session 3 teaches the trap by name. At the next retrain, score the book's
training accounts with out-of-fold probabilities, so that the watchlist and the tier counts on
the existing book are out-of-sample. Until then, read the watchlist as a list to review, never
as evidence of accuracy (a prohibited use, [7.1](purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses)). **Owner:**
model developer, with the portal owner (proposed; to be named).

## Finding 3 — The capture gate is met narrowly {#ews-finding-3}

**Finding.** The model clears its binding gate by a handful of accounts, and on resampling the
held-out accounts about a quarter of the time it would not.

**Evidence.** On the held-out accounts ([7.5](performance.qmd#how-firm-each-result-is)): the
top decile holds {{< var ews.capture_events >}} of the {{< var ews.n_events_holdout >}}
deteriorations, and the gate needs {{< var ews.gate.capture_events_needed >}}, a margin of
{{< var ews.gate.capture_events_margin >}} accounts, {{< var ews.gate.capture_margin_pp >}}
percentage points. The bootstrap 95% interval, {{< var ews.boot.capture.lo >}} to
{{< var ews.boot.capture.hi >}}, contains the {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}} gate, and
{{< var ews.boot.capture_below_gate >}} of {{< var ews.boot.n >}} resamples fall below it.

The gate was also set at development, with the model's performance in view. The master spec
asked for more; `ews/docs/enhancement_notes.md` records what it asked for and why it was not
kept:

```text
Because AUC ≥ 0.75 and top-decile capture ≥ 3× are unreachable on this data, the build gates
on what the data genuinely supports: **top-decile capture ≥ 2× lift** and **PR-AUC > base
rate**, with AUC reported (not gated).
```

The ceiling bears that out: on the held-out accounts even the generator's noise-free logit
reaches AUC {{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}} and captures
{{< var ceiling.ews.latent_capture_holdout >}}, below both of the master spec's targets
([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-ceiling)). Re-specifying was necessary. Under the platform's gate
policy ([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd#gate-policy)) the level is set to the guideline as calibrated
to what the data support ([7.9](gate.qmd#history)); it is not derived from the ceiling and sits
close to what the model achieved, which is why the narrow margin is a finding.

**Impact.** The gate's verdict is sensitive to the sample. A retrain on a fresh draw of the
same book, or the first cohorts in monitoring, could fall below the gate with nothing wrong
with the model, and a single-cohort breach rule would then fire on noise. Conversely, the
pass is not strong evidence that the model would pass again. The bootstrap understates the
spread: it resamples the held-out rows with the model held fixed, so the variation from drawing
a different split and refitting the model is not in the {{< var ews.boot.capture_below_gate >}}.
The PR-AUC gate, which is met
firmly, does not compensate: it asks only for a ranking better than none
([7.7](limitations.qmd#ews-observations)).

**Compensating control.** Report the capture interval and the margin beside the gate on every
run; the facts recompute both on every `verify.py`. In monitoring, a cohort below the gate is
a review; two consecutive cohorts below it trigger redevelopment ([7.8](monitoring.qmd)). At
redevelopment, estimate capture over repeated splits or cross-validation rather than one split.
The gate is not changed by this finding, and is never relaxed to let a model pass
([7.9](gate.qmd)). **Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 4 — Not distinguishable from the score alone on AUC {#ews-finding-4}

**Finding.** Ranked by the scorecard's PD alone, the held-out accounts come out about as well
as the model ranks them. The behavioural model's gain over the score it consumes is not
established.

**Evidence.** On the held-out accounts ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-benchmark)): AUC
{{< var ews.auc >}} for the model and {{< var ews.pd_score.auc >}} for `pd_score` alone. Over
{{< var ews.boot.n >}} paired bootstrap resamples, the model's lead is
{{< var ews.pd_score.diff >}}, with a 95% interval from {{< var ews.pd_score.diff_lo >}} to
{{< var ews.pd_score.diff_hi >}}: it contains zero. On capture, `pd_score` alone reaches
{{< var ews.pd_score.capture >}}, below the gate, where the model reaches {{< var ews.capture >}};
that difference has no interval, and finding 3 shows how wide the model's own is. By gain the
scorecard's two columns carry {{< var ews.importance.score_gain_share >}} of the model
([7.3](methodology.qmd#ews-importance)), which says how the trees spread their splits, not
what the model would lose without the score.

**Impact.** Early Warning's case rests on the behaviour since booking adding something to
what was known at origination. On this sample that is not shown on AUC, and shown on capture
only by one comparison with no interval. D4's findings reach this model through the score
([7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-the-score-is-a-valid-input)). Nothing here says the model is
worse than the score; it says no one should claim it is better.

**Compensating control.** The facts report the benchmark on every `verify.py` run. At
redevelopment, before the behavioural model is kept, compare it with `pd_score` alone on
capture and AUC with paired intervals, and refit it without the score
([7.6](sensitivity.qmd#reduced-input-refits-not-run)). Until then, make no claim that Early
Warning ranks better than the score alone. **Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 5 — The Low tier under-predicts {#ews-finding-5}

**Finding.** Among held-out accounts in the Low tier, more deteriorate than the model's
probability says, by more than the calibration tolerance, on enough events to count.

**Evidence.** By tier, on the held-out accounts ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-tiers-held-out)): the Low
tier's {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.n >}} accounts include {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.events >}}
deteriorations, an observed rate of {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.observed >}} against a mean
probability of {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.predicted >}}: observed / predicted
{{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.ratio >}}, outside the {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}} to
{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}} tolerance, on more than the {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}
events the floor requires. High ({{< var ews.tier_ho.High.ratio >}}) and Medium
({{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.ratio >}}) are inside it. The probability is `predict_proba`'s,
with no calibration step ([7.3](methodology.qmd#the-model-lightgbm)); an over-fitted model
pushing quiet-looking accounts towards zero is consistent with the miss, but that cause is not
measured.

**Impact.** The tier is still a ranking, and the Low tier still deteriorates least, so review
priority is not affected. Any use of the probability as a rate is: an expected count of
deteriorations in the Low tier, which holds {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.recall >}} of held-out
deteriorations, would be too low.

**Compensating control.** At the next retrain, add a calibration step fitted on rows the trees
were not fitted on (Platt or isotonic on out-of-fold probabilities). Until then, never read
`prob` as a deterioration rate (a prohibited use, [7.1](purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses)), and
monitor observed / predicted by tier on each cohort with matured outcomes against the floor
([7.8](monitoring.qmd)). **Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 6 — The configured delinquency clause can never fire {#ews-finding-6}

**Finding.** The `DELINQUENCY` trigger is configured as "days past due at or above a
threshold", with a second clause, "any days past due in the most recent quarter", written into
the code. On this data the configured clause can never fire, so every delinquency flag comes
from the clause no configuration controls.

**Evidence.** Over the {{< var ews.n_book >}} booked accounts
([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-trigger-performance)):

| Clause | Threshold and its source | Largest value over the book | Accounts it fires on by itself |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dpd_max >=` | {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.threshold >}}, `EWS_TRIGGERS["{{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.config_key >}}"]` | {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.feature_max >}} | {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.n_alone >}} |
| `dpd_recent >` | {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_recent.threshold >}}, {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_recent.config_key >}} in `triggers.py` | {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_recent.feature_max >}} | {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_recent.n_alone >}} |

The trigger fires on {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.n >}} accounts
({{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.share >}} of the book), every one through `dpd_recent`. The
generator explains it: each month's days past due is a Poisson draw whose mean scales with the
true PD (`shared/data_generator.py`), so the counts stay small:

```python
dpd_lambda = np.clip(pd_true * 30 * (1 + 0.5 * (cur > 0.9)), 0, None)   # shared/data_generator.py
days_past_due = rng.poisson(dpd_lambda * 0.1).astype(int)
```

The one unit test of the triggers, `tests/test_triggers_and_rules.py::test_triggers_fire_by_name`,
fires `DELINQUENCY` through `dpd_max` alone, with `dpd_recent` at zero: it tests the clause
that never fires and not the one that always does. The workbench shows a slider for
`dpd_severe` ([7.6](sensitivity.qmd#trigger-thresholds)); moving it anywhere above the data's
maximum changes nothing.

**Impact.** An untested control and an unconfigurable one in the same rule. The live clause is
not hidden — `shared/config.py` mentions it in a comment beside `dpd_severe`, and the workbench
shows both clauses — but it appears there only in a comment: its threshold is not a key in
`EWS_TRIGGERS`, and no configuration can change it. A reviewer adjusting the configuration can
move only the clause that never fires; on this data delinquency is flagged at a day past due,
on half the book. The
trigger loses most of its meaning as a warning sign, which finding 7 measures.

**Compensating control.** At the next policy review, restate the severe-delinquency threshold
on this data's scale, or remove the clause and say so; move the `dpd_recent` threshold into
`EWS_TRIGGERS` so the live clause is configured and visible; and add a unit test in which
`dpd_recent` alone fires. Until then, the facts count every clause's firings by itself on each
`verify.py` run ({{< var ews.trigger.n_dead_clauses >}} dead clause today), and the monitoring
plan flags any clause that fires on no account ([7.8](monitoring.qmd#ews-trigger-monitoring)).
**Owner:** monitoring policy owner (proposed; to be named), with the model developer for the
code.

## Finding 7 — The triggers beat the base rate only modestly and fire on most of the book {#ews-finding-7}

**Finding.** Each trigger flags accounts that deteriorate only modestly more often than
average, and together they flag most of the book. As an alert, a trigger carries little
information; as a reason attached to a tier, it still names something real.

**Evidence.** From [7.5](performance.qmd#ews-trigger-performance), with lift over the book's
base rate of {{< var ews.base_rate >}}:

- precision from {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.precision >}} (`DELINQUENCY`, lift
  {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.lift >}}×) to {{< var ews.trigger.high_utilization.precision >}}
  (`HIGH_UTILIZATION`, lift {{< var ews.trigger.high_utilization.lift >}}×) on the held-out
  accounts — all below {{< var ews.gate.lift_min >}}×, against {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.lift >}}×
  for the High tier;
- any trigger fires on {{< var ews.trigger.any.n >}} accounts, {{< var ews.trigger.any.share >}}
  of the book; a flagged held-out account deteriorates at {{< var ews.trigger.any.precision >}},
  an unflagged one at {{< var ews.trigger.none.rate >}};
- `DELINQUENCY`, in effect "any days past due" (finding 6), alone flags
  {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.share >}} of the book.

**Impact.** A list of triggered accounts is most of the book and is only slightly richer in
deteriorations than the book itself, so it cannot be worked as a call list. Most triggered
accounts — {{< var ews.overlap.triggered_not_high.share >}} — are not High
([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-tiers-and-triggers)). The thresholds were never set against this
book's distribution ([7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-trigger-thresholds-are-generic)), and the
sweep that would set them has not been run ([7.6](sensitivity.qmd#trigger-thresholds)).

**Compensating control.** At the next policy review, run the threshold sweep and re-set each
threshold against this book's distribution, with a stated precision or lift target for a
trigger to be kept. Until then, present triggers as reasons attached to a tier — which is how
the portal and the workbench show them — never as a standalone alert list, and monitor each
trigger's fire rate and precision ([7.8](monitoring.qmd#ews-trigger-monitoring)).
**Owner:** monitoring policy owner (proposed; to be named).

## Finding 8 — The label shares the features' window, so lead time is unmeasured {#ews-finding-8}

**Finding.** Early Warning exists to warn before trouble shows — before a missed payment
([7.1](purpose.qmd)). On this data the label is drawn over the same months the features
summarise, so how far ahead the model warns has never been measured.

**Evidence.** The generator draws `{{< var ews.target >}}` once, from the true PD, utilisation
over the panel's last quarter, the rise in utilisation from the panel's first month to its last,
and leverage ([7.2](data.qmd#ews-label)); there is no period after the panel. Several features
measure the label's own drivers over the same months: `util_recent` and `utilization_onbook` are
the recent utilisation, and `util_drift` measures the same rise. Train and held-out are random
splits of one cohort, so there is no out-of-time sample either — the same gap D4 finding 1
records for the scorecard ([7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-the-label-looks-forward)).

**Impact.** Every performance figure in [7.5](performance.qmd) measures same-window
classification, not early warning. On a real book the label would come after the features, part
of the behaviour driving it would happen in that gap, and capture across a real horizon would
plausibly be lower; it is not measured. A claim that the model gives a review team months of
notice rests on nothing in this chapter. This is a property of the synthetic data, not a defect
in the code, but it goes to the model's stated purpose, so it is a finding, as D4's equivalent
is.

**Compensating control.** Before any claim of lead time, measure capture out of time on the
first cohort whose outcomes mature after its features were taken; the monitoring plan's first
capture reading is that test ([7.8](monitoring.qmd)). Until then, treat every figure as
same-window classification, and never claim that the model warns ahead of a missed payment (a
prohibited use, [7.1](purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses)). **Owner:** model developer.

## Observations {#ews-observations}

Recorded but not raised as findings. Each is a design choice stated here so it can be
challenged, a property of the synthetic data, minor on this data, or covered by a control
above.

| Observation | Evidence | Why not a finding | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUC is low in absolute terms | Held-out AUC {{< var ews.auc >}}; a reference LightGBM, configured as the committed one and given every observable column, reaches {{< var ceiling.ews.oracle_model.auc >}} on the same accounts, and the noise-free logit {{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}} ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-ceiling)) | The model is indistinguishable from the reference model, and even the noise-free logit is low: the data's noise caps any ranking. That does not show no better model exists. Gating on capture with AUC reported is the design answer ([7.9](gate.qmd)) | Keep reporting AUC beside the ceiling on every run; never compare it with an origination model's AUC |
| The PR-AUC gate asks only for a ranking better than none | A ranking without information scores about the base rate; the gate is PR-AUC above the base rate, met by {{< var ews.pr_auc_over_base >}} times, with {{< var ews.boot.pr_auc_at_or_below_base >}} of resamples at or below it ([7.5](performance.qmd#how-firm-each-result-is)) | Firmly met; capture is the binding gate | Report PR-AUC as a multiple of the base rate, so a fall shows before the gate fails |
| Some High-tier accounts carry no trigger | {{< var ews.overlap.high_no_trigger.n >}} of the {{< var ews.tier.High.n >}} High-tier accounts on the book; {{< var ews.overlap.high_no_trigger_ho.n >}} among the held-out ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-tiers-and-triggers)) | The layers are independent by design; those accounts still carry SHAP reasons in the v1 account view and the workbench | Review them on their SHAP reasons and history; count them in monitoring |
| Two features are structural zeros for this target | `industry` and `entity_type` play no part in how the generator draws deterioration; neither is in the top {{< var ews.importance.top_n >}} by gain ([7.3](methodology.qmd#ews-importance)) | Present but inert, as in D4 (D4 finding 3) | Remove at the next redevelopment |
| A missing panel fires no trigger | Missing features become zero in `compute_ews_features`; with the committed thresholds zero fires no trigger; the model's probability for such an account is not computed ([7.6](sensitivity.qmd#reduced-input-refits-not-run)) | The generated data have a full history for every account | Refer an account with missing history to a reviewer in any production use, rather than score it |
| No leakage test of Early Warning's features in the test suite | `tests/test_leakage.py` checks the scorecard and adjudication only ([7.2](data.qmd#leakage-controls)) | The deny-list is enforced on every feature build and at training, so every `verify.py` run checks it | Add the test at the next change to `ews/` |
| `pd_score` is in-sample for the scorecard on most booked accounts | The scorecard's training rows were drawn from all applicants, without regard to booking ([7.2](data.qmd#ews-score-input)) | Fitted on a different label by a binned additive model with little room to memorise; small, and not measured | Measure with out-of-fold scores at the next redevelopment of either model |
| No check ties the panel cache to `panel.parquet` | `verify.py`, the portal and the facts score the model on the committed `ews/models/panel_features.parquet`; nothing re-aggregates `panel.parquet` and compares ([7.9](gate.qmd#where-they-are-recomputed-independently)) | The cache is a committed artifact, so any change to it shows in a commit's diff | Add a check that re-aggregates the panel and compares it with the cache, under `verify.py --full`, at the next change to `ews/` |
